Concept Involved:
1. When cells are connected in series, their internal resistances always add up, regardless of the polarity of the cells.
2. When a cell is wrongly connected (reversed polarity) in a series combination, its EMF opposes the EMFs of the correctly connected cells, effectively reducing the net EMF by 2ε for each reversed cell.
Solution:
1. Effective Internal Resistance (r0): All N internal resistances are in series. r0 = N ⋅ r
2. Effective EMF (ε0):
Number of correctly connected cells = N – n.
Number of wrongly connected cells = n.
The EMF of each wrongly connected cell subtracts from the total. The effective EMF of the n wrong cells is –nε.
Alternatively, each reversed cell cancels the EMF of one correctly connected cell and also reduces the overall EMF by its own EMF. The net decrease in EMF for n reversed cells is 2nε (one ε from the reversed cell and one ε from the cell it effectively cancels).   
Final Answer: (3)"
